---
title: "Projected change of thermal indices: WorldClim CMIP6"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, dpi = 96,
                      out.width = "100%")
library(thermify)
province <- read.csv("data/cc-cauquenes-province.csv")
stations_cc <- read.csv("data/cc-ceaza-stations.csv")
stations <- read.csv("data/ceaza-stations.csv", encoding = "UTF-8")
index_label <- c(gdd = "Degree-days (base 10 degC)",
                 ch = "Chilling hours (0-7.2 degC)", cu = "Utah chill units",
                 cp = "Chill portions (Dynamic)")
unit <- c(gdd = "degC day", ch = "h", cu = "units", cp = "portions")
ssp_label <- c("245" = "SSP2-4.5", "585" = "SSP5-8.5")
```

How much would degree-days and winter chill change by mid-century? This page
uses the WorldClim 2.1 downscaled CMIP6 projections, read with
`worldclim_future_region()`, for **14 global climate models (GCMs)**, two
scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) and the period **2041-2060**, against the
WorldClim 1970-2000 baseline.

> **Read these numbers as changes, not as future values.** The validation
> with observed stations
> ([CEAZA-Met article](validation-ceaza.html)) showed that WorldClim and
> monthly climatologies have large errors for chill, so this page reports
> the **change** between the future and the baseline of the same data,
> where much of that error cancels. It also reports the spread between
> models: a single GCM can be far from the consensus.

Scripts: `data-raw/climate-change/`. Heat season 1 September - 30 April;
chill season 1 May - 31 August.

## Province of Cauquenes (Maule)

Indices computed with `thermify_rast()` from the monthly WorldClim surfaces
(degree-days with the averaging method; chill with the Linvill hourly
reconstruction, `ch_methods = "hourly"`).

```{r province-table}
base <- province[province$ssp == "baseline", ]
rows <- list()
for (s in c("245", "585")) for (ix in names(index_label)) {
  b <- base$value[base$index == ix]
  d <- province$value[province$ssp == s & province$index == ix] - b
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    Scenario = ssp_label[[s]], Index = index_label[[ix]],
    Baseline = sprintf("%.0f %s", b, unit[[ix]]),
    `Median change` = sprintf("%+.0f (%+.0f %%)", stats::median(d),
                              100 * stats::median(d) / b),
    `Range of 14 GCMs` = sprintf("%+.0f to %+.0f", min(d), max(d)),
    check.names = FALSE)
}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, rows), row.names = FALSE, caption = paste(
  "Province mean, 2041-2060 against 1970-2000. Baselines are WorldClim",
  "values and inherit their errors; use the changes."))
```

```{r maps, fig.height = 7}
prov <- cauquenes_boundary("provincia", crs = "EPSG:4326")
ix_show <- c("gdd", "ch", "cp")
pal <- list(gdd = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
            ch = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "Blues", rev = FALSE),
            cp = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "Blues", rev = FALSE))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 5))
for (s in c("245", "585")) for (ix in ix_show) {
  r <- terra::rast(sprintf("data/cc-cauquenes-%s-ssp%s.tif", ix, s))
  rng <- range(unlist(lapply(c("245", "585"), function(ss) {
    terra::minmax(terra::rast(sprintf("data/cc-cauquenes-%s-ssp%s.tif",
                                      ix, ss))[["median_change"]])
  })))
  terra::plot(r[["median_change"]], col = pal[[ix]], range = rng,
              axes = FALSE, mar = c(1, 1, 3, 5),
              main = sprintf("%s\n%s (%s)", ssp_label[[s]],
                             sub(" \\(.*", "", index_label[[ix]]),
                             unit[[ix]]), cex.main = 0.95)
  terra::lines(prov)
}
par(op)
```

Median change across the 14 GCMs, 2041-2060. For degree-days, chilling
hours and Utah units all 14 models agree on the sign of the change in every
cell. For chill portions they do not everywhere: in the coldest fifth of the
province (winter mean temperature of about 6-8 degrees C) the median change
is close to zero, sometimes slightly positive, and the models split; in the
rest every model projects a loss, larger where winters are milder. This is
expected from the Dynamic model, in which chill accumulates most efficiently
at moderate temperatures: a cold site can lose little chill, or even gain
some, from a moderate warming.

### The choice of chill model changes the conclusion

Under the same warming, **chilling hours fall by about half, but chill
portions fall by less than a tenth**. Chilling hours count every hour
between 0 and 7.2 degrees C and ignore that slightly warmer hours still
contribute to chill accumulation; the Dynamic model, which describes chill
accumulation and its reversal by heat, responds much less to a moderate
warming. Studies that report future chill only as chilling hours therefore
tend to overstate the loss (Luedeling et al. 2011). For planning,
**prefer chill portions**, and report chilling hours only for comparison
with older literature.

## CEAZA-Met stations (north-central Chile): delta method

At 29 of the 30 stations of the [validation](validation-ceaza.html), each model's
monthly change at the station's WorldClim cell is applied to **every hour
of the station's observed record**: the shift goes
from the change of the minimum at the daily minimum to the change of the
maximum at the daily maximum. The indices are then computed from the
modified hourly series, season by season, exactly as the reference of the
validation. This keeps the observed day-to-day and year-to-year variability,
and the present-day baseline is the observed index.

The change applied is each model's change **from the period of the record
to 2041-2060**, not from 1970-2000: the records cover about 2004-2025 and
already contain part of the warming since 1970-2000, which would otherwise
be counted twice. WorldClim gives each model's change from 1970-2000
(centred on 1985) to each future period; the change at the record's
midpoint (about 2015) is interpolated linearly between 1985 and the model's
2021-2040 change and subtracted. The model's own trajectory is used, not
the observed warming, because the two differ: in the semi-arid north the
historical series shows almost no winter warming since 1970-2000, while the
models warm winters, and mixing both would exaggerate the projected loss
of chill. Punta de Choros is
excluded: the station is on the shoreline and its WorldClim cell is sea
(no data), so there is no model change to apply.

A simpler variant, adding the change to the station's monthly climatology,
is **not** used: monthly climatologies lose the cold nights, give zero chill
portions at several interior stations that actually accumulate 27-31
portions per season, and make marginal sites lose all their chill under any
warming.

```{r stations, fig.height = 5}
st <- merge(stations_cc, stations, by = "station")
gcm_median <- stats::aggregate(
  cbind(baseline, change) ~ station + name + elevation + ssp + index,
  data = st, FUN = stats::median)
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (ix in c("gdd", "cp")) {
  d <- gcm_median[gcm_median$index == ix, ]
  rel <- ifelse(abs(d$baseline) > 1e-9, 100 * d$change / d$baseline, NA)
  cols <- ifelse(d$ssp == 245, "#0B5563", "#E8702A")
  plot(d$elevation, rel, pch = 21, bg = adjustcolor(cols, 0.75),
       col = "white", cex = 1.3, las = 1, xlab = "Station elevation (m)",
       ylab = "Median relative change (%)", main = index_label[[ix]],
       cex.main = 0.95)
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey50")
  legend(if (ix == "gdd") "topright" else "bottomright",
         legend = ssp_label, pt.bg = c("#0B5563", "#E8702A"), pch = 21,
         col = "white", pt.cex = 1.3, bty = "n")
}
par(op)
```

Each point is a station and scenario (median of the 14 GCMs).

```{r stations-table}
d <- gcm_median
d$rel <- ifelse(abs(d$baseline) > 1e-9, 100 * d$change / d$baseline, NA)
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("245", "585"), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(index_label), function(ix) {
    x <- d[d$ssp == as.integer(s) & d$index == ix, ]
    data.frame(Scenario = ssp_label[[s]], Index = index_label[[ix]],
               `Median over stations` = sprintf("%+.0f %%",
                 stats::median(x$rel, na.rm = TRUE)),
               `Stations losing all chill` = if (ix == "gdd") "-" else
                 as.character(sum(x$baseline > 0 & x$baseline + x$change <= 0)),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
warm <- stats::aggregate(cbind(delta_tmin, delta_tmax) ~ ssp,
                         data = stations_cc, FUN = stats::median)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, caption = sprintf(paste(
  "Median relative change over the stations (each station: median of 14",
  "GCMs). Median warming at the stations from the record period to",
  "2041-2060: SSP2-4.5 %+.1f degC (Tmin) and %+.1f degC (Tmax); SSP5-8.5",
  "%+.1f and %+.1f degC."),
  warm$delta_tmin[warm$ssp == 245], warm$delta_tmax[warm$ssp == 245],
  warm$delta_tmin[warm$ssp == 585], warm$delta_tmax[warm$ssp == 585]))
```

Because the changes are measured from the period of the records (about
2015), the warming applied at the stations, about +1.0 degrees C under
SSP2-4.5 and +1.4 degrees C under SSP5-8.5, is smaller than in the
Cauquenes maps, which are measured from 1970-2000. Even so, the semi-arid
north loses a larger share of its chill: the median station loses about
**a fifth of its chill portions** (19 % under SSP2-4.5, 25 % under
SSP5-8.5), against less than a tenth in Cauquenes for a larger warming.
Under SSP2-4.5 the losses are largest on the coast (about 37 % at Coquimbo
and Caleta El Toro and 31-33 % at La Serena, below 170 m) and smallest at
the highest station (4 % at Los Molles, 2,543 m). No station loses all its chill
portions. Chilling hours fall by about a third at the median station and
disappear only at Caleta El Toro under SSP5-8.5, where the observed
baseline is below 2 hours per season. Utah units can be negative because
the Utah model subtracts chill for warm hours, so their relative changes
are unstable near zero and exceed -100 % at some stations; use them with
care in mild climates.

## Through time: historical series and four scenarios

The figure below follows degree-days and chill portions through time, in
the style of the CMIP6 projection plots of Brunner et al. (2020), for four
scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5) and the four 20-year
periods of WorldClim (2021-2040 to 2081-2100). WorldClim provides 20-year
means, not yearly projections. Each model's trajectory is therefore drawn
through its four period means, placed at the centre of each period (2030,
2050, 2070 and 2090), from a common starting point (the WorldClim
1970-2000 value, centred on 1985, for the province; the observed mean,
centred on the record's midpoint, for the station), with a monotone
spline; the curves end in 2090, the centre of the last period. The line is
the median of the models' trajectories and the shaded band the likely
range (17th to 83rd percentile, 66 % of the models), year by year. The
curves describe the climate around each year, not a forecast of
individual years: unlike yearly model runs, they carry no year-to-year
variability, which the historical and observed series show.

* **Cauquenes (left).** The historical series 1951-2023 comes from the
  WorldClim 2.1 historical monthly weather data (CRU-TS 4.09 downscaled
  with WorldClim, 2.5 arc-minutes), and the projections from the CMIP6
  surfaces; all values are computed with the same monthly method from the
  province-mean temperatures, so the past and the projections are directly
  comparable. As monthly-based estimates, their absolute values carry the
  biases measured in the validation.
* **Vicuna (right; CEAZA-Met, Elqui valley, 634 m).** The historical series
  1951-2023 at the station's WorldClim cell (same monthly method as for the
  province), the observed seasons of the station's hourly record, and
  projections with the delta method on that record. Each model's change is
  taken from the period of the record (centred on about 2015) to each
  future period, so that the warming already contained in the record is
  not counted twice. All three are shown as **relative change from
  2005-2023**, the period of the record: the historical series and the
  observed record differ in level (about 76 chill portions per season at
  the 2.5-arc-minute cell with the monthly method, against 37 observed at
  the station; the cell averages about 4.6 km of terrain around a station
  on the valley floor, and the monthly method has its own biases), so only
  their changes and variability are comparable.

```{r timeseries, fig.height = 7.5}
ts_prov <- read.csv("data/cc-timeseries-cauquenes.csv")
ts_vic <- read.csv("data/cc-timeseries-vicuna.csv")
ssp_cols <- c("126" = "#1D3354", "245" = "#D4A20B", "370" = "#F21111",
              "585" = "#840B22")
ssp_names <- c("126" = "SSP1-2.6", "245" = "SSP2-4.5", "370" = "SSP3-7.0",
               "585" = "SSP5-8.5")
period_span <- function(p) as.numeric(strsplit(p, "-")[[1]]) + c(0, 1)

ts_panel <- function(d, ix, title, ylab, xlim = c(1950, 2101)) {
  d <- d[d$index == ix, ]
  proj <- d[d$source == "projection", ]
  past <- d[d$source %in% c("historical", "observed"), ]
  past <- past[order(past$year), ]
  rng <- range(c(past$value, proj$value), na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = rng + c(-0.04, 0.04) * diff(rng),
       xlab = "", ylab = ylab, main = title, las = 1, cex.main = 1,
       panel.first = abline(h = pretty(rng), col = "grey92"))
  base <- d[d$source == "baseline", ]
  # Starting point shared by all models: the WorldClim 1970-2000 value
  # (centred on 1985) for the province, the observed mean (centred on the
  # record's midpoint) for a station.
  anchor <- if (nrow(base)) c(1985, base$value) else
    c(mean(past$year), mean(past$value))
  from <- if (nrow(base)) 2015 else anchor[1]
  years <- seq(from, 2090, by = 0.5)
  for (s in names(ssp_cols)) {
    traj <- lapply(unique(proj$gcm[proj$ssp == s]), function(g) {
      v <- proj[proj$ssp == s & proj$gcm == g, ]
      if (nrow(v) < 4) return(NULL)
      x <- c(anchor[1], vapply(v$period, function(p) mean(period_span(p)) - 0.5, 1))
      f <- stats::splinefun(x, c(anchor[2], v$value), method = "monoH.FC")
      f(years)
    })
    traj <- do.call(rbind, traj)
    if (is.null(traj) || nrow(traj) < 3) next
    q <- apply(traj, 2, stats::quantile, c(0.17, 0.5, 0.83))
    polygon(c(years, rev(years)), c(q[1, ], rev(q[3, ])), border = NA,
            col = adjustcolor(ssp_cols[[s]], 0.2))
    lines(years, q[2, ], col = ssp_cols[[s]], lwd = 2.2)
  }
  if (nrow(base)) segments(1970, base$value, 2001, base$value, lwd = 2,
                           lty = 2, col = "grey30")
  if (any(past$source == "historical")) {
    lines(past$year, past$value, col = "grey35", lwd = 0.8)
    sm <- stats::filter(past$value, rep(1 / 11, 11), sides = 2)
    lines(past$year, sm, lwd = 2.4, col = "black")
  } else {
    points(past$year, past$value, pch = 21, bg = "white", cex = 0.9)
    segments(min(past$year), mean(past$value), max(past$year) + 1,
             mean(past$value), lwd = 2.4)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Station panel in relative change (%) from the record period, so that the
# WorldClim historical series (monthly method, 2.5-arc-minute cell) and the
# observed hourly record, which differ in level, can be compared in trend
# and variability.
ts_panel_rel <- function(d, ix, title, ylab, ref = 2005:2023,
                         xlim = c(1950, 2101)) {
  d <- d[d$index == ix, ]
  hist <- d[d$source == "historical", ]
  hist <- hist[order(hist$year), ]
  obs <- d[d$source == "observed", ]
  obs <- obs[order(obs$year), ]
  proj <- d[d$source == "projection", ]
  obs_mean <- mean(obs$value)
  rel_hist <- 100 * (hist$value / mean(hist$value[hist$year %in% ref]) - 1)
  rel_obs <- 100 * (obs$value / obs_mean - 1)
  proj$value <- 100 * (proj$value / obs_mean - 1)
  anchor <- c(mean(obs$year), 0)
  years <- seq(anchor[1], 2090, by = 0.5)
  bands <- list()
  for (s in names(ssp_cols)) {
    traj <- lapply(unique(proj$gcm[proj$ssp == s]), function(g) {
      v <- proj[proj$ssp == s & proj$gcm == g, ]
      if (nrow(v) < 4) return(NULL)
      x <- c(anchor[1], vapply(v$period, function(p) mean(period_span(p)) - 0.5, 1))
      stats::splinefun(x, c(anchor[2], v$value), method = "monoH.FC")(years)
    })
    traj <- do.call(rbind, traj)
    if (!is.null(traj) && nrow(traj) >= 3)
      bands[[s]] <- apply(traj, 2, stats::quantile, c(0.17, 0.5, 0.83))
  }
  rng <- range(c(rel_hist, rel_obs, unlist(bands)), na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = rng + c(-0.04, 0.04) * diff(rng), xlab = "",
       ylab = ylab, main = title, las = 1, cex.main = 1,
       panel.first = abline(h = pretty(rng), col = "grey92"))
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey60")
  for (s in names(bands)) {
    q <- bands[[s]]
    polygon(c(years, rev(years)), c(q[1, ], rev(q[3, ])), border = NA,
            col = adjustcolor(ssp_cols[[s]], 0.2))
    lines(years, q[2, ], col = ssp_cols[[s]], lwd = 2.2)
  }
  lines(hist$year, rel_hist, col = "grey35", lwd = 0.8)
  lines(hist$year, stats::filter(rel_hist, rep(1 / 11, 11), sides = 2),
        lwd = 2.4, col = "black")
  # Observed seasons as a curve, broken where a season is missing.
  full <- seq(min(obs$year), max(obs$year))
  y <- rel_obs[match(full, obs$year)]
  lines(full, y, col = "#0B8FA3", lwd = 1.6)
  points(obs$year, rel_obs, pch = 16, cex = 0.55, col = "#0B8FA3")
  invisible(NULL)
}

n_models <- function(d, s) {
  length(unique(d$gcm[d$source == "projection" & d$ssp == s]))
}

op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3, 4.5, 2.5, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 0, 0))
ts_panel(ts_prov, "gdd", "Cauquenes (province mean)",
         "Degree-days, base 10 degC")
ts_panel_rel(ts_vic, "gdd", "Vicuna (CEAZA-Met, 634 m)",
             "Degree-days, change from 2005-2023 (%)")
ts_panel(ts_prov, "cp", "", "Chill portions")
ts_panel_rel(ts_vic, "cp", "", "Chill portions, change from 2005-2023 (%)")
par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0),
    new = TRUE)
plot.new()
legend("bottom", ncol = 3, bty = "n", cex = 0.82, inset = 0.005,
       legend = c(paste0(ssp_names, " (",
                         sapply(names(ssp_names), n_models, d = ts_prov),
                         " GCMs)"),
                  "WorldClim historical, 11-yr mean", "WorldClim 1970-2000",
                  "CEAZA-Met observed seasons"),
       col = c(ssp_cols, "black", "grey30", "#0B8FA3"),
       lwd = c(6, 6, 6, 6, 2.4, 2, 1.6),
       lty = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1),
       pch = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 16), pt.cex = 0.6)
par(op)
```

```{r timeseries-numbers}
hist_mean <- function(ix, years) {
  h <- ts_prov[ts_prov$source == "historical" & ts_prov$index == ix, ]
  mean(h$value[h$year %in% years])
}
proj_median <- function(d, ix, s, p) {
  stats::median(d$value[d$source == "projection" & d$index == ix &
                          d$ssp == s & d$period == p])
}
obs_mean <- function(ix) mean(ts_vic$value[ts_vic$source == "observed" &
                                             ts_vic$index == ix])
gdd_70s <- hist_mean("gdd", 1971:1980)
gdd_10s <- hist_mean("gdd", 2011:2020)
cp_base <- ts_prov$value[ts_prov$source == "baseline" & ts_prov$index == "cp"]
cp_hist <- hist_mean("cp", 1970:2000)
vic_cp <- obs_mean("cp")
```

What the figure shows:

* **Degree-days have already risen.** In Cauquenes the historical series
  rises from `r round(gdd_70s)` degree-days in 1971-1980 to
  `r round(gdd_10s)` in 2011-2020 (`r sprintf("%+.0f %%", 100 * (gdd_10s / gdd_70s - 1))`),
  and the 2021-2040 projections continue that trend. After mid-century the
  scenarios separate: by 2081-2100 the median reaches
  `r round(proj_median(ts_prov, "gdd", "126", "2081-2100"))` degree-days
  under SSP1-2.6 and
  `r round(proj_median(ts_prov, "gdd", "585", "2081-2100"))` under
  SSP5-8.5.
* **Chill has not yet changed in Cauquenes, but it will under high
  emissions.** Chill portions have stayed near
  `r round(cp_hist)` per season since 1951. Under SSP1-2.6 they hardly
  change (`r round(proj_median(ts_prov, "cp", "126", "2081-2100"))` in
  2081-2100); under SSP5-8.5 they fall to `r round(proj_median(ts_prov, "cp", "585", "2081-2100"))`
  by 2081-2100.
* **The semi-arid north is far more exposed.** At Vicuna the observed mean
  is `r round(vic_cp)` chill portions per season; by 2081-2100 the median
  is `r round(proj_median(ts_vic, "cp", "126", "2081-2100"))` under SSP1-2.6
  and `r round(proj_median(ts_vic, "cp", "585", "2081-2100"))` under
  SSP5-8.5, too few for most temperate fruit trees. The scenario chosen
  matters far more than the model: the bands of SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 do
  not overlap after 2060.

* **Monthly data hide the year-to-year variability of chill.** At Vicuna
  the historical series and the observed seasons agree on degree-days
  (year-to-year standard deviation of about 6 % and 5 % in 2005-2023), but
  the observed chill portions vary far more than the monthly series (21 %
  against 8 %): monthly means smooth out the cold spells that drive chill
  accumulation. The historical series also shows that degree-days at
  Vicuna have risen by about 12 % since 1971-1980, while chill has not
  changed.

Two details are worth reading correctly. The WorldClim 1970-2000 value of
chill portions (`r round(cp_base)`) is higher than the mean of the
historical seasons over the same years (`r round(cp_hist)`), while for
degree-days both agree: the Dynamic model is non-linear, and the index of
a mean climate is not the mean of the indices of individual years. The
projections are built on the WorldClim climatology, so compare them with
the dashed line rather than with single historical seasons. Second, the
interpolation between period centres is a smooth guide, not a model
result in its own right: only the values at 2030, 2050, 2070 and 2090 come
from the projections.

## Limitations

* **Changes, not forecasts.** WorldClim future surfaces add each model's
  change to the 1970-2000 baseline; the results describe a climate
  centred on 2041-2060, not any particular year.
* **Monthly data in Cauquenes.** The province maps are computed from
  monthly climatologies, which lose day-to-day variability and bias absolute
  chill values (about -25 % for chilling hours in the validation); changes
  are less affected but not immune. The station analysis avoids this by
  using the observed hourly records, but assumes that day-to-day and
  diurnal variability stay as they are.
* **Model spread.** The table shows the range of 14 GCMs; some (for
  example CanESM5 and UKESM1-0-LL) warm more than most models. The median
  is the summary to use.
* **Baseline period.** The Cauquenes maps and table measure changes from
  1970-2000, part of which has already happened. The station analysis
  measures them from the period of each record, interpolating each model's
  trajectory between 1985 and 2021-2040; this assumes that the model's
  warming is roughly linear over those decades.
* **Validation.** Chill estimates have been validated only in semi-arid
  north-central Chile; the central-south is pending.

## References

Luedeling, E., Girvetz, E. H., Semenov, M. A., & Brown, P. H. (2011).
